# Changes made after the first drafts (read this before you fix your chapters)

The first drafts of the report and the KT pack were written against the code as it was at 10:00 on 21 October 2026. These changes were made afterwards. Re-read the named files, then make every chapter you wrote true of the code as it is now. Do not describe a fixed problem as still open, and do not describe an unfixed one as fixed.

## Code that changed (all in `finalsem/project`)
1. **Copied page markers are removed from answers.** `stripPageMarkers()` in `src/core/prompts.js`, used in `src/engines/local.js`. Two unit tests. The Intel summary in `docs/test-runs/v2-local-intel.json` and the screenshot `v2-intel-short-popup.png` were recorded BEFORE this change and still show the marker: say so ("recorded before the fix").
2. **The popup tells the user when the small model took over.** For a finished summary whose `stats.modelSwitchReason` is `GPU_MEMORY` or `MODEL_LOAD_FAILED`, the result block shows (element `#result-notice`): "The main model did not fit in the graphics card, so the smaller model wrote this summary. It may be less detailed." No notice for `integrated-graphics` (that case has the graphics note). The model line is now refreshed once when any job ends, success or error (`refreshModelLineOnce` in `src/ui/popup.js`), so after both models fail it no longer shows a stale "Not downloaded yet". The job record's `notice` field is still always null (the new notice is computed in the popup from the stats). Browser scenario V10 checks the notice. The screenshots ui-12 and ui-13 were re-shot after this change and show it.
3. **No "Downloading" label for a stored model.** `mapInitProgress(report, {cached})` in `src/core/gpu-check.js`; `src/offscreen/offscreen.js` checks `hasModelInCache` before loading. Real-model check after the fix: `docs/test-runs/v2-local-nvidia-offline-after-label-fix.md` (17.7 s short, 16 s two-part, first answer written at 65 tokens a second, no "Downloading" line; load took 11.6 s). The earlier clean offline run (`v2-local-nvidia-offline.md`: 15.3 s and 16.5 s) was made before the fix and has the wrong line at 3.9 s; keep citing it for timings and say so. Unit test added.
4. **The offscreen page is never closed while a message is running.** `src/background/offscreen-manager.js` counts messages in flight; only the last one to finish starts the 5-minute idle countdown, and `close()` does nothing while any message is running. One unit test.
5. **A job counts as dead after 5 minutes without an update, not 3** (`STALE_MS` in `src/background/service-worker.js` and `src/ui/popup.js`). The 180-second answer timeout (`generateTimeoutMs`) is unchanged. Version 1 kept 3 minutes.
6. **`oom` matches only as a whole word** in `src/core/engine-errors.js` ("room" is not an out-of-memory error). Unit test.
7. **Dead CSS removed** from `src/ui/ui.css` (key box and options page rules). One small rule added for the notice spacing.
8. **`scripts/set-chrome-gpu.ps1`**: `-ChromePath` is now optional (the script finds Chrome itself), so `powershell -File scripts\set-chrome-gpu.ps1 -Remove` works as written in the README. **`setup.bat --gpu`** now prints "The graphics setting was NOT changed ..." if the script fails (setup still goes on). New script check B10c.
9. **`scripts/check-computer.ps1`** prints "Free space on drive C: ..." (the double colon is gone).

# Second change list (24 October 2026): a failure in the real Chrome, and what it led to

The project owner ran the extension in the real Chrome on the developer laptop (Intel graphics chip, so SmolLM2) on the Wikipedia "Lighthouse" page and got "Something went wrong inside the extension. Try again." with no reason. A hidden run of the same case failed with TIMEOUT. The causes found, and the changes, are below. DEVLOG row dated 2026-10-24 tells the story. Make every chapter true of the code as it is now.

## Code that changed
1. **New error code `CONTEXT_TOO_LONG`** (now 15 codes, was 14). WebLLM refuses a prompt that does not fit the 4096-token window with the text "Prompt tokens exceed context window size ..."; before, `classifyEngineError` did not know that text and the user saw the vague SERVICE_ERROR message. Message shown only if cutting the part in half also fails: "A part of this page is too long for the model to read at once, even after it was cut in half. Try a shorter page."
2. **Halve and retry (this was "not built"; it is built now).** In `src/engines/local.js`, `summarizeChunk` catches CONTEXT_TOO_LONG, cuts the part in half at a paragraph or sentence break (`chunkText`) and summarizes each half; up to 3 levels deep, not for text under 600 characters. A page that was a single part becomes two parts plus one merge request. `stats.halvedParts` counts the cut parts. Unit tests: 4 new. Browser scenario V25 uses the new pretend-model mode `longprompt`.
3. **The answer time limit is 10 minutes, not 180 seconds** (`generateTimeoutMs` 600000 in `src/core/config.js`). Reason: on the Intel chip one answer took more than 180 s in the failing run (parts took 76 s, 127 s and then more than 180 s). The TIMEOUT message is unchanged. Wherever a chapter says "three minutes" or "180 seconds" for the answer limit, it is 10 minutes now.
4. **Heartbeat.** The offscreen page's KEEPALIVE message (every 10 s while it works) now also refreshes `updatedAt` of every running job record (`src/background/service-worker.js`). Without it a single answer longer than the 5-minute dead-job limit would show as "interrupted" while still running. Browser scenario V26 checks it (a 16 s pretend answer).
5. **Technical detail in the popup.** For SERVICE_ERROR and MODEL_LOAD_FAILED the popup shows a small line under the message: "Technical detail: ..." (first 240 characters of the error detail, element `#error-detail`). So the vague message is no longer a dead end. Browser scenario V27 uses the new pretend-model mode `crash`.
6. **Pretend-model modes are now 12:** ok, nowebgpu, nof16, intel, oom, oomall, downloadfail, empty, html, slow, longprompt, crash.
7. **Real-run script** `scripts/local-run.mjs`: new plans `intel-wikipedia` and `intel-short`; it now deletes the profile's `Service Worker` and `Code Cache` folders before launching, because a persistent profile kept an OLD service worker script (the new `halvedParts` stat was missing from a real run made after the code changed; found by comparing the saved stats with the source). The downloaded model is not touched (it lives in IndexedDB). Consequence to state honestly: real-model runs made before 24 October ran the service-worker-side code as it was when each profile was first used; changes made later to service-worker files (marker stripping, idle close, 5-minute limit) are covered by unit and browser tests but were not exercised by a real-model run until the Intel Wikipedia run noted below.

## Test counts now
Unit tests: 76. Browser tests: 29 (smoke, V01 to V27, V18b). Windows script checks: 15. Say "76", "29", "15".

## Real runs on the Intel chip with the Wikipedia article (7 parts of 6,000 characters, 36,752 characters of text)
- `docs/test-runs/v2-local-intel-wikipedia-before-fix.md`: TIMEOUT after 615.6 s. Part 6 of 7 started at 435.8 s and had not answered 180 s later. Parts took 76 s (part 1), 127 s (part 2), 66 s, 50 s, 77 s. Old code.
- `docs/test-runs/v2-local-intel-wikipedia-second-try-old-code.md`: the same old code finished on the second try: summary in 704.5 s, part times 75 s, 124 s, 73 s, 56 s, 90 s, 121 s, 60 s, merge 100 s. Same code, same page, different result: answer times vary a lot on this chip, so a limit of 180 s was too tight.
- `docs/test-runs/v2-local-intel-wikipedia.md`: the run with the new code (after the stale service-worker scripts were cleared; its stats include `halvedParts: 0`): summary in 616.4 s, part times 70.6, 68.4, 65.9, 75.1, 79.2, 121.5 and 68.6 s, merge about 62.7 s, writing speed 4.1 tokens a second. No part overflowed the window on that day, so the halving did not trigger in a real run; it is covered by the unit tests and scenario V25 only. Page text on Wikipedia changes from day to day, so a part that overflows one day may fit the next.
- Whatever a chapter says about a long page on the Intel chip: it takes about 10 to 12 minutes for the 7-part Lighthouse article with SmolLM2 (616.4 s with the new code, 704.5 s with the old code), and the summaries are of poor quality. CORRECTION: the invented facts are in the summary of the OLD-code second try (`v2-local-intel-wikipedia-second-try-old-code.json`: a "1901" gas light named "Dalén light" with "Agamassan (Aga)" as substrate, "the 1611 lighthouse" three times, a "1939 National Historic Lighthouse Preservation" sentence; do not quote them as facts). The NEW-code run's summary (`v2-local-intel-wikipedia.json`) is three short generic points (history and significance; a list of 14,700 lighthouses; 54 diagrams and 651 photographs) whose counts were not checked against the page.

## Still true
Everything in the "Still true" paragraph of the first change list, except: halve-and-retry is built; the TIMEOUT path is still not covered by an automated test (the pretend model has no timeout); the dead-job rule stays at 5 minutes.


# Third change list (26 October 2026): speed on the client's laptop

The client sent photos of the laptop (see `finalsem/docs/CLIENT_LAPTOP.md`, facts only): HP Laptop 15-fd0xxx, Core i7-1355U, 16 GB, **Intel Iris Xe built-in graphics only (no separate card)**, 363 GB free, Chrome 156.0.8078.48, WebGPU hardware accelerated. So the built-in graphics path is THE path for the client. The owner said 10 minutes for a page is far too long and asked for it to be optimised as much as possible, a bigger model being fine if it fits. This list REPLACES any earlier statement that conflicts with it. Decision D7 in `finalsem/docs/DECISIONS.md` has the reasoning, the question put to Opus and its answers. The DEVLOG row dated 2026-10-26 tells the story. Numbers below come from the files named.

## Facts that are no longer true (find and fix every one in your chapters)
- "On built-in graphics the extension picks SmolLM2 360M by itself" (decision D3) is **removed**. The main model Llama 3.2 1B is now the default everywhere, including built-in graphics. SmolLM2 is used only (a) when the person chooses Quality: Fast in the popup's Settings, (b) after a memory or load failure with the main model (saved `modelOverride`, as before), (c) when the browser reports under 8 GB of memory. `modelSwitchReason` is `quality-fast` for (a). `chooseModel({deviceMemoryGB, override, quality})`.
- "The client's laptop details were requested and have not come back" is now: the details came back (CLIENT_LAPTOP.md); the extension has still NOT been run on that laptop or in a visible Chrome window.
- "A long page takes 10 to 12 minutes on the Intel chip" is now true only for **Read the whole page**. The default takes about 2 minutes (below).
- `setup.bat --gpu` has nothing to do on the client's laptop (one graphics chip).
- Test counts: 93 unit tests, 31 browser scenarios, 15 script checks. Pretend modes: still 12.
- The unit test and browser scenario V09 (integrated graphics) now expect the main model (Llama 3.2 1B) with the Intel note; new scenario V29 checks that Settings > Quality: Fast switches to SmolLM2 and is remembered; new scenario V28 checks a shortened long page and the whole-page button.

## What was built (all in `finalsem/project`)
1. **Where the time goes (measured).** `scripts/bench-models.mjs` and `docs/test-runs/bench-models.md` (+ `.json`): on built-in Intel graphics reading the page (prefill) is about 80 percent of the time of a part, and reading speed is low whatever the model: SmolLM2-135M 40, SmolLM2-360M 26 to 29, Qwen2.5-0.5B 24 to 33, Llama 3.2 1B 15.6 tokens a second; writing: 13.6, 4.7, 3.5 and 2.6, 2.0 tokens a second; one realistic part: 43 s, 66 s, 54 s and 47 s, 162 s. The q4f32 versions are no faster at reading and slower at writing. gemma3-1b did not load (a window configuration error in this WebLLM version). Qwen2.5-1.5B was not measured (run stopped). All hidden Chromium, developer laptop's Intel Gen-12 chip, one run per model.
2. **Cut what is not worth reading** (`src/core/trim-text.js`, `cleanPageText`): the back matter (a heading See also / References / Notes / Bibliography / External links ... that starts after 40 percent of the page and at least 800 characters in) and markers such as [12], [a], [edit], [citation needed]. On the Lighthouse page: 8,788 of 36,752 characters (24 percent). `stats.trimmedChars`.
3. **Shorten a long page before reading, on built-in graphics** (`src/core/condense.js`, `condenseText`; the engine's `readBudgetChars()` says 6,000 characters on built-in graphics and 0 = everything elsewhere; settings `readBudgetIntegrated` 6000 and `readBudgetOther` 0): the opening in full (35 percent of the budget), then the first sentences of the paragraphs, evenly spread over the page, with the headings of the kept sections. The result is exactly one part, so there is no merge request. `stats.textChars` (after cleanup), `stats.readChars`, `stats.condensed`, `stats.estimateFullSeconds` (a rough guess from the measured speed). Pure functions with unit tests (`tests/unit/condense.test.js`, `trim-text.test.js`).
4. **The popup says so and offers the whole page:** after a shortened summary it shows "This is a long page. To keep it quick on this computer, the opening of each section was read: about N% of the text. Reading all of it would take roughly M minutes." (element `#condense-notice`) and a link-style button "Read the whole page (slower)" (`#read-all`), which starts a job with `full: true` (no shortening). The stats line says "read N% of the text".
5. **Short answers on built-in graphics** (`brief` prompts in `src/core/prompts.js`): single part 3 short sentences (limit 130 tokens, `briefTokensSingle`), part of a long page 2 sentences (90, `briefTokensPart`), merge 4 or 5 sentences (180, `briefTokensMerge`), plain text. A fast card keeps the richer format and the old limits (320 and 300). When the model was stopped by the length limit (`finishReason: 'length'`, now returned by the offscreen page) the answer is cut back to its last full stop (`endAtSentence`).
6. **Settings > Quality** in the popup (a closed `<details id="settings">`, select `#quality`): "Better: Llama 3.2 1B (more accurate, slower)" or "Fast: SmolLM2 360M (about 2 times quicker, but summaries are often muddled or wrong)". Stored as `quality` in chrome.storage.local.
7. **Preload:** when the popup opens on a normal page and the chosen model is already stored, the popup sends `PRELOAD_MODEL`; the service worker loads and warms the model (about 35 s of warm-up on the Intel chip) so the first answer does not wait for it. It never downloads. The offscreen page now unloads a loaded model before loading a different one (quality change).
8. **Cleaner answers:** `stripPageMarkers` now also removes a repeated copy of the prompt's own safety sentence and an empty "Summary:" label, so such an answer becomes EMPTY_ANSWER ("The model returned no summary for this page.") instead of showing the prompt. Seen with SmolLM2 on the Wikipedia page.
9. Scripts: `scripts/bench-models.mjs`, `scripts/dump-page-text.mjs` (what the extension reads from a page), `scripts/local-run.mjs` plans `intel-better` (Llama default, 3 cases), `intel-fast` (Quality: Fast), `intel-wikipedia`, `intel-short`.
